hints: Form the line through $A$ and $B$ using direction $\overrightarrow{AB}=(2,3,-1)$.
Equate its coordinates to those of $l$ and solve the $x$- and $y$-component equations for the two parameters.
Substitute those parameter values into the $z$-component equation to determine $m$.
walkthrough:
Find the direction vector $\overrightarrow{AB}$ from $A(1, -2, 2)$ to $B(3, 1, 1)$:
$$\overrightarrow{AB} = \overrightarrow{OB} - \overrightarrow{OA} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix} = 2\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j} - \mathbf{k}$$

Write the vector equation of the line passing through $A$ and $B$ using parameter $\lambda$:
$$\mathbf{r}_{AB} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} + \lambda \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 + 2\lambda \\ -2 + 3\lambda \\ 2 - \lambda \end{pmatrix}$$

Write the parametric coordinates of line $l$:
$$\mathbf{r}_l = \begin{pmatrix} 2 + \mu \\ 1 - 2\mu \\ m - 4\mu \end{pmatrix}$$

Equate corresponding components of the two lines at their intersection:
$$\text{x-component}: \quad 1 + 2\lambda = 2 + \mu \implies 2\lambda - \mu = 1 \quad \text{--- (1)}$$
$$\text{y-component}: \quad -2 + 3\lambda = 1 - 2\mu \implies 3\lambda + 2\mu = 3 \quad \text{--- (2)}$$
$$\text{z-component}: \quad 2 - \lambda = m - 4\mu \quad \text{--- (3)}$$

Solve equations (1) and (2) for $\lambda$ and $\mu$:
From (1), $\mu = 2\lambda - 1$.
Substitute into (2):
$$3\lambda + 2(2\lambda - 1) = 3 \implies 3\lambda + 4\lambda - 2 = 3 \implies 7\lambda = 5 \implies \lambda = \dfrac{5}{7}$$
Then find $\mu$:
$$\mu = 2\left(\dfrac{5}{7}\right) - 1 = \dfrac{10}{7} - \dfrac{7}{7} = \dfrac{3}{7}$$

Substitute $\lambda = \dfrac{5}{7}$ and $\mu = \dfrac{3}{7}$ into equation (3) to find $m$:
$$2 - \dfrac{5}{7} = m - 4\left(\dfrac{3}{7}\right)$$
$$\dfrac{9}{7} = m - \dfrac{12}{7} \implies m = \dfrac{9}{7} + \dfrac{12}{7} = \dfrac{21}{7} = 3$$

hints: The plane contains the direction $\overrightarrow{AB}=(2,3,-1)$ and is parallel to $(1,-2,-4)$.
Find a normal perpendicular to both directions using a vector product or two scalar-product equations.
Substitute the actual point $A=(1,-2,2)$ into $ax+by+cz=d$, then simplify the whole equation by a common factor.
walkthrough:
Identify two non-parallel direction vectors lying in or parallel to the plane:
$$\mathbf{d}_1 = \overrightarrow{AB} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{d}_2 = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix}$$

Compute the normal vector $\mathbf{n}$ using the cross product $\mathbf{d}_1 \times \mathbf{d}_2$:
$$\mathbf{n} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} (3)(-4) - (-1)(-2) \\ (-1)(1) - (2)(-4) \\ (2)(-2) - (3)(1) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -12 - 2 \\ -1 + 8 \\ -4 - 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -14 \\ 7 \\ -7 \end{pmatrix}$$

Divide by the common factor $-7$ to choose a simpler normal vector:
$$\mathbf{n} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -1 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$$

Write down the Cartesian form of the plane equation:
$$2x - y + z = d$$

Substitute the coordinates of point $A(1, -2, 2)$ to find the constant $d$:
$$d = 2(1) - (-2) + 2 = 2 + 2 + 2 = 6$$

State the final Cartesian equation of the plane:
$$2x - y + z = 6$$
